1.title: Course Introduction and Exam Orientation
1.text: Welcome to this exam prep course for the A W S Cloud Practitioner exam, whose code is C L F dash C zero two. This first module is the orientation. It covers the exam itself, what is in scope, how to read the exam guide, and how this course works. There are no practice questions here; the questions start in Module one.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do five things. Describe the exam: its length, its question types, and how it is scored. Say what the exam guide covers, and why you should read the current version. Name the four domains and their weights. Know who the exam is for, and what it leaves out. And use the tags, the case, the Design Checks and the practice questions of this course.

1.title: Case Check-In: Meet Tidewater Outfitters
1.text: Meet Tidewater Outfitters, a fictional online shop for outdoor gear, run by a small team. Its founder wants everyone to understand the cloud well enough to make sound choices. The shop is moving from a rented server room to A W S, one decision at a time. You will follow each decision: access, security, storage, databases, networks and costs. Your job in this course is to learn what each A W S service is for, and when to choose it.

1.title: The Exam at a Glance
1.text: Here is the exam in six numbers. There are sixty-five questions in total. Fifty are scored, and fifteen are unscored trial questions that A W S uses to test new items. You cannot tell which are which, so treat every question as real. You have ninety minutes, which is about eighty-three seconds a question across all sixty-five. Your result is a scaled score from one hundred to one thousand, and seven hundred passes. Exam tip: the fifteen unscored questions are not marked on screen, so give every question your full attention.

1.title: Question Types and Scoring
1.text: There are two question types. Multiple choice has one correct answer and three distractors. Multiple response has two or more correct answers out of five or more options, and the question tells you how many to pick. An unanswered question counts as wrong, and there is no penalty for guessing, so answer every one. Scoring is compensatory, which means you must pass the exam as a whole, not each section. The section feedback on your score report is general, and A W S says to read it with care. One thing the guide does not say is how multiple-response questions are marked. Exam tip: never leave a question blank.

1.title: Booking, Taking and Keeping the Credential
1.text: Now the practical details. The fee is one hundred U S dollars, with possible extra costs such as exchange rates. You can take the exam at a Pearson view test center, or online with a proctor. It is offered in several languages, including English. The Italian and German versions retire after the thirty-first of December, twenty twenty-six. The credential is valid for three years, and you can renew it by passing the latest version of the exam, or an Associate or Professional exam. There are no prerequisites. As of the fourth of November, twenty twenty-six, check A W S's certification page for price, languages and delivery. Exam tip: fees, languages and renewal rules change, so read A W S's page before you book.

1.title: The Exam Guide Is Your Scope
1.text: The exam guide is your scope. It lists the domains, the weights, the task statements and the in-scope services. This course follows version one point three, published on the twenty-ninth of October, twenty twenty-six. The guide had four versions in twenty twenty-six: on the twenty-fourth of June, the twenty-eighth of August, the twenty-fourth of September, and the twenty-ninth of October. A W S publishes changes about a month before they reach the exam. The service list is non-exhaustive and subject to change. So the guide outranks this course on scope. Exam tip: read the current exam guide before you book, and again in the last week.

1.title: Four Domains, Nineteen Task Statements
1.text: The exam has four domains. Domain one, Cloud Concepts, is twenty-four percent of scored content, with four task statements. Domain two, Security and Compliance, is thirty percent, with four. Domain three, Cloud Technology and Services, is thirty-four percent, with eight task statements. Domain four, Billing, Pricing, and Support, is twelve percent, with three. That makes nineteen task statements. The weights are shares of scored content, and the guide gives no weights below the domain level. Exam tip: domains one and two together are more than half of the exam.

1.title: Who the Exam Is For
1.text: Who is the exam for? The target candidate has up to six months of exposure to A W S Cloud design, implementation or operations. That might be someone early in a cloud career, or someone who works with people in cloud roles. The exam is foundational and not tied to a job role. The guide lists what is out of scope for the candidate: coding, designing cloud architecture, troubleshooting, implementation, and load and performance testing. And the task statements use verbs such as define, identify and understand. Exam tip: learn what each service is for and when to choose it; setting it up step by step is not what is tested.

1.title: How This Course Works
1.text: Here is how this course works. There are seventeen modules: this introduction, fourteen content modules in the guide's order, a recap, and an exam-technique module. Each content module has what you will learn, a Tidewater case, Exam Tips, a recap and practice questions. Each also has a Design Check, and a few have an optional Try it lab. Slides carry four tags: Beyond the guide, Old name, Verify live, and Dates. About one question in five is multiple response in this course. That share is this course's choice, not A W S's, because the guide does not publish one.

1.title: Independent Course, Official Sources
1.text: A word on independence. This course is not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Amazon Web Services. It shows no A W S logos or service icons, and service names appear as text. The notes and questions are in our own wording, and the course uses no A W S exam questions or exam dumps. A W S documentation and the exam guide outrank this course on every fact and rule. Names, prices and limits change, so check the source on every Verify-live slide. Exam tip: when this course and the current documentation disagree, the documentation wins.

1.title: Your Study Plan and Ground Rules
1.text: Your study plan and ground rules. Study one module, then do its questions; the modules follow the exam guide's order. Cover every task statement, because the guide does not weight them separately. Read the exam guide before you book, and again in the last week. On the day, answer all sixty-five questions and never leave one blank. And remember that this course is independent and educational, so the official sources outrank it. Exam tip: before you book, read A W S's current exam guide and certification page. That is the orientation. In Module one we start with the value of the A W S Cloud.
